page.layout: One column of verse, centred on the page; below it the colophon "Libri secundi / finis."; below that a woodcut ornament with no text.

main_text.l: Per maria ire paras, quid si deserta ferarum,
Saxaque Cannibalum fugeres? tua Regna relinquis,
Meque fugis, saltem, ah, si te fastidia nostri
Tanta tenent, spacium precor, exiguamque furenti
Da requiem, dum speratos perferre dolores
Fortius edificam, non tu cum nostra subires
Littora, & ignotos intrares aduena portus.
Bella tuli, & prima vetui confidere terra:
At si nulla tuae tangit te cura salutis,
Firmaque adhuc animo sententia perstat eundi,
Me quoque fer tecum, & spumosas tolle per undas;
Hoc precor, exiguum hoc munus moritura reposco.
Talibus orantem, lacrimis immobilis Heros
Multa dolens, & egramque animi miseratus amantem,
Deserit. At postquam facientem vela Columbum
Illa videt, certumque abitus correpta dolore
Exanimis cadit, atque oculos nox plurima presfit;
Excipiunt famulae, manibusque intecta reportant
Regia, pallentem, ac gelido sudore fluentem,
Et tacitos imo quaestus sub corde cientem.
Libri secundi
finis.

page.notes: Woodcut ornamental headpiece at the foot, with no text. The verse is Virgil, Aeneid IV, lines 1 to 28 approximately, in italic type. Line "Exanimis cadit, atque oculos nox plurima presfit;" is printed with a long-s form, which I have read as "pressit" with the s-form and given as printed. The colophon is in roman type, with "finis." in italic.
